ontology.note: Emits an fw:NetworkReachability activity carrying fw:originCount, fw:reachedNodeCount, fw:travelBudgetMetres, fw:travelBudgetMinutes, fw:assumedSpeedMetresPerMinute, fw:travelDirection and fw:edgeLengthSource, and prov:used the site source. The budget is asserted in metres as well as minutes, with the speed beside it, because the minutes are the metres divided by one assumed speed and a reader must be able to divide back out. No fw:metricCRS: this activity re-measures no geometry, so fw:edgeLengthSource names where the lengths came from instead.

changes.description: Street junctions within a travel budget of an origin, each carrying the budget left on arrival. Extracted from the Dijkstra inside isochrone (src/catchments.ts:76) unchanged, including the edge reversal that makes inbound a different question from outbound. Fourth of six primitives an isochrone composition needs. Settles the carrier question that stopped the decomposition in experiment 82: the truncation downstream consumes budget minus cost at the edge's start node, which is a per-node quantity, so reached junctions travel as points with a remainingM attribute and no lines port type is needed. The corridor step that follows truncates by remainingM over lengthM and never restates the minutes or the speed. Takes no UTM zone, unlike the eight metric widgets: costs are the network's own lengthM values and nothing here re-measures geometry. See docs/experiments/83-reachable-junctions.md.

evidence.note: Eleven unit checks cover junctions inside a 200 m budget being returned and a 300 m one not; travelled plus remaining equalling the budget at every junction; the cheapest route deciding the cost, where a 400 m direct street loses to 100 plus 100 through a third junction; inbound and outbound differing on a one-way street in both directions; an origin without a networkNodeId failing with a message naming the snap step; an origin snapped to a different network being refused rather than dropped; per-origin sets tagged by origin; the constant speed and the trusted street lengths both appearing in the notes; a node beyond the budget being discovered but never settled; and refusal of an impossible budget, speed, direction or label. One check runs the real composition: snapping then reachability over the 738-node Soho network the John Snow example ships, at its own 5 minutes and 75 m per minute, reaching 142 junctions. Not established: that the reached set is what anyone can actually reach. Parity against NetworkX ego_graph with distance='length' is not done.
